Title: Introduction to operations management
Description: For staff new to operations roles: explains what operations management does in an organisation, how inputs are transformed into goods and services, and how processes can be designed and improved.

Title: Understanding operations management
Description: For managers and planners with some operations background: examines how operations strategy, process design and performance objectives such as quality, speed, cost and flexibility shape an organisation's output.

Title: Supply chain sustainability
Description: For buyers, planners and managers: introduces how supply chains work and how environmental and social sustainability can be built into sourcing, production and logistics decisions.

Title: Project management: the start of the project journey
Description: For people starting to lead projects: covers how projects are defined and initiated, including scoping, stakeholders, planning and the early decisions that set a project up to succeed.

Title: Project governance and Project Management Office (PMO)
Description: For experienced project staff and managers: looks at how organisations govern projects and what role a project management office plays in oversight, standards and reporting.

Title: Managing virtual project teams
Description: For team and project leads working across sites or countries: explores how to plan, communicate with and build trust in teams that collaborate mainly through digital tools.

Title: Working in groups and teams
Description: For team members and new leaders: explores group dynamics, team roles and practical ways to improve collaboration and handle problems within working groups.

Title: Managing and managing people
Description: For new and aspiring managers: introduces what managers do day to day and the core skills of managing people, including motivation, delegation and working relationships.

Title: Understanding management: I'm managing thank you!
Description: For anyone wanting to organise their own work better: introduces ideas and practical techniques for self-management, such as planning time, priorities and personal effectiveness.

Title: Making decisions
Description: For managers and team leaders: explains different approaches to decision-making in organisations, common biases and pitfalls, and techniques for making better-informed choices.

Title: The importance of interpersonal skills
Description: For all staff: covers core interpersonal skills such as listening, questioning and non-verbal communication, and how they affect working relationships and results.

Title: Developing high trust work relationships
Description: For supervisors and managers: explores why trust matters at work and practical ways to build and repair trust with colleagues, teams and partners.

Title: Difference and challenge in teams
Description: For team leaders: looks at how differences in background, views and working styles create both conflict and opportunity in teams, and how to manage them constructively.

Title: Three principles of a coaching approach
Description: For supervisors and managers who want to coach their staff: introduces the core principles of a coaching style of management and how to apply them in everyday conversations.

Title: Effective communication in the workplace
Description: For employees at any level: covers the basics of effective workplace communication, including choosing channels, writing and speaking clearly, and listening well.

Title: Understanding your customers
Description: For sales, merchandising and customer-facing staff: explains core marketing concepts for understanding customers, including how consumer and business-to-business buying differ.

Title: Risk management
Description: For managers and specialists: introduces how organisations identify, assess and respond to business risks, drawing lessons from well-known risk management failures.

Title: Employee engagement
Description: For HR staff and line managers: explains what employee engagement is, why it matters for performance and retention, and how managers can influence it.

Title: Diversity and inclusion in the workplace
Description: For managers and HR staff: introduces workplace diversity and inclusion, why it matters, and practical steps to create fairer and more inclusive teams.

Title: Workplace learning with coaching and mentoring
Description: For supervisors, trainers and HR staff: looks at how to plan and manage workplace learning and talent development, using coaching and mentoring.

Title: Collective leadership
Description: For managers and team leads: explores how leaders and followers work together and how shared, collective approaches to leadership can make leaders more effective.

Title: Leadership challenges in turbulent times
Description: For experienced managers: examines the challenges leaders face during uncertainty and change and approaches for leading people through disruption.

Title: Using data to aid organisational change
Description: For managers and analysts: explores how data and evidence can be gathered and used to understand problems and support organisational change decisions.

Title: Business communication: writing a SWOT analysis
Description: For staff who write business documents: shows how to research and write a clear SWOT analysis and present the findings in a structured business style.

Title: Facilitating group discussions
Description: For supervisors and meeting leads: covers the skills needed to plan and facilitate productive group discussions and meetings.

Title: Fundamentals of cost accounting and environmental management accounting
Description: For finance and operations staff: introduces cost accounting concepts and how environmental costs can be tracked and managed to support sustainable production decisions.

Title: Sustainable innovations in enterprises
Description: For managers interested in sustainability: explores how businesses innovate their products and processes to reduce environmental and social impacts.

Title: Introduction to business agility
Description: For supervisors and managers driving change: a brief look at what business agility means and how teams can respond faster to shifting conditions, with hands-on activities.

Title: Decision trees and dealing with uncertainty
Description: For managers and analysts: introduces basic probability and shows how decision trees help compare options and make decisions under uncertainty, using financial examples.

Title: Hybrid working: change management
Description: For managers leading change: covers how to plan and manage organisational change, with a focus on the shift to hybrid ways of working.

Title: AI fluency
Description: For business users new to AI: a short learning path covering AI basics, responsible use (including deepfakes and copyright concerns) and getting started with Microsoft Copilot.

Title: Integrated safety, health and environmental management: An introduction
Description: For supervisors, HSE staff and managers: shows how an organisation can bring safety, health and environmental management together into a single integrated system, covering risk assessment and compliance.

Title: Presenting information
Description: For staff who report numbers: shows how to carry out simple calculations and present numerical information clearly in tables and charts.

Title: Systems thinking and practice
Description: For staff tackling complex problems: introduces systems thinking concepts and diagramming techniques for understanding situations with many interacting parts.

Title: Data analysis: hypothesis testing
Description: For staff who analyse data: introduces the logic of hypothesis testing and how to apply common statistical tests to decide whether differences in data are meaningful.

Title: Data analysis: visualisations in Excel
Description: For spreadsheet users: shows how to summarise and visualise data in Excel using charts and descriptive statistics.

Title: Manufacturing
Description: For production and engineering staff: introduces manufacturing processes and how materials, process choice and design decisions affect how products are made.

Title: Assessing risk in engineering, work and life
Description: For supervisors and technical staff: explains how risks are identified, estimated and judged in engineering and everyday work, and how to reason about acceptable risk.

Title: Groups and teamwork
Description: For technical staff working in project teams: covers how engineering groups work together, team roles and practical ways to improve teamwork.

Title: Health and safety in the laboratory and field
Description: For staff working in labs, testing rooms or on site: a short introduction to hazard awareness, risk assessment and safe working practices.

Title: Introducing technology and innovation management
Description: For managers: introduces how organisations manage technology and innovation, from spotting opportunities to adopting new processes and products.

Title: Exploring data: Graphs and numerical summaries
Description: For staff who work with numbers: introduces ways to describe data sets using graphs and numerical summaries such as mean, median and spread.

Title: Interpreting data: Boxplots and tables
Description: For staff who read reports and data: explains how to interpret boxplots and tables to compare data sets and spot patterns.

Title: Working with charts, graphs and tables
Description: For staff building numeracy: covers how to read, interpret and create charts, graphs and tables used in everyday work.

Title: Design thinking
Description: For staff involved in improvement or product work: introduces design thinking as a structured, creative approach to understanding problems and developing solutions.

Title: An introduction to intercultural competence in the workplace
Description: For staff working with colleagues and customers from other cultures: introduces intercultural competence and practical ways to communicate across cultural differences.

Title: Leadership and followership
Description: For current and emerging leaders: explores the relationship between leaders and followers and how both roles shape effective leadership.

Title: Work and mental health
Description: For managers and HR staff: explores the links between work and mental health and how workplaces can support people with mental health difficulties to stay in or return to work.

Title: Environmental management and organisations
Description: For managers and operations staff: introduces how organisations manage their environmental impacts, including environmental management systems and reporting.

Title: Organisations, environmental management and innovation
Description: For managers and improvement staff: examines how organisations use environmental management and innovation to reduce their environmental footprint.
